subject: Post-call: SDK onboarding + throttling constraints for IntegraHealth POC
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: Suresh Patel <suresh.patel@integrahealth.com>, Megan Ross <megan.ross@integrahealth.com>
Cc: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-10-21T15:04:00-07:00
Subject: Post-call: SDK onboarding + throttling constraints for IntegraHealth POC

Hi Suresh / Megan —

Thanks again for taking the time today. Quick recap and concrete next steps so we stay aligned for the POC: we focused on SDK onboarding, auth options, request routing (multi-region), and behavioral constraints around embeddings and reranking. Below are the action items we discussed and a few clarifying questions for your team.

POC goals (agreed):
- Validate end-to-end pipeline: user text -> embedding -> reranker -> structured tool-calling output.
- Measure tail latency for inference at 20 QPS steady-state, with bursts to 50 QPS.
- Validate data controls (no customer PII persisted in hosted logs).

Immediate asks for IntegraHealth:
1) Confirm preferred auth method: API key scoped to project OR service-account OAuth (we recommended API key for fastest onboarding).
2) Confirm network requirements: IP ranges to whitelist, and whether you require a Private VPC/private deployment. You mentioned a corporate firewall — please attach the network diagram and allowed egress list.
3) Typical request shape: expected tokens per request (prompt + expected completion), and top 5 test prompts you'll run.
4) Embedding usage: are you doing single-document embeddings or batch indexing? Estimate batch sizes and how often you re-index.

Operational constraints we highlighted (please confirm):
- Target steady QPS: 20 per app integration; acceptable burst to 50 for short periods (~30s).
- Latency SLO target: p95 generation < 400ms for short-form outputs, p95 for reranking flows < 600ms.
- Retry expectations: client should implement exponential backoff with jitter; include deterministic request IDs.

Attachments: SOW draft + network checklist attached (Integra_POC_SOW_v1.pdf, network_checklist.xlsx).

Next steps:
- You: send network diagram and preferred auth choice by EOD Friday (2026-10-23).
- Us: Jordan will drop a minimal SDK setup snippet for embedded auth + interceptor that injects X-Request-ID; Ben will sketch routing rules for region fallback; I'll follow up with a short runbook for 429 handling and idempotency.

If anything above doesn't match your understanding, call it out and we'll correct. Otherwise let's aim to kick off the technical onboarding on Monday.

Thanks,
Marissa

Subject: Re: Post-call: SDK onboarding + throttling constraints for IntegraHealth POC

Marissa — thanks for the clear recap. A few clarifications from our side: 

1) Auth: we'd prefer API keys scoped per-environment (dev/stage/prod). We will rotate keys via our secrets manager.
2) Network: attaching our current network diagram (integra_network_diagram.png). We will need to whitelist Redwood egress IP ranges — I'll confirm the exact CIDRs by tomorrow.
3) Load profile: steady-state ~20 QPS per integration with short bursts up to 60 QPS for up to a minute during batch index jobs. Peak batch embedding jobs will send batches of ~500 documents (we expect to window them).
4) Embeddings: we'll do batched indexing nightly; real-time embeddings for smaller flows (1-5 docs). We want guidance on batching size vs latency tradeoffs.
5) Idempotency: for batch jobs we can provide a job_id; for single-requests we'll include a client-generated request_id. Can you confirm Redwood's recommended header names and retention of those IDs in logs for debug?

Also — question on 429 handling: if a large batch run hits a token-level throttle, do you prefer clients to back off and replay at a slower rate, or accept partial success with per-item retry? For our use case, partial success + per-item retry would be preferable, but only if error visibility is clear.

I'll send the CIDRs and a sample of our embedding job payload tomorrow.

Thanks,
Suresh

IntegraHealth

Date: 2026-10-21T18:02:00-07:00
Subject: Fwd: Post-call: SDK onboarding + throttling constraints for IntegraHealth POC

Team — forwarding Suresh's note and the network diagram. Quick tech ask list for the onboarding workstream; Jordan/Ben please take ownership and flag anything that needs product/infra exceptions. Rishi, FYI on SLOs and logging.

Key integration/architecture asks (from the call and Suresh):
- Auth: API key per-environment; keys rotated by customer. Ensure SDK supports easy key rotation via an interceptor.
- Routing: prefer region_us primary with auto-fallback to region_eu only if latency spikes; need to document routing policy and behavior under capacity.
- Structured/tool calling: we will expose a single tool for 'patient_lookup' which must accept a structured JSON schema and return deterministic outputs. We should provide a sample structured-output schema and JSON schema validation in the SDK.
- Embeddings/reranker: recommend batching strategy — suggest batches of 64–256 depending on payload size. For nightly bulk indexing (500 docs), recommend splitting into smaller windows of 100 with backoff between windows.
- 429 handling & retries: implement exponential backoff with full jitter. Suggested algorithm: base=200ms, cap=60s, max attempts=6. For batch endpoints we should support per-item retry status so clients can replay failed items rather than re-sending whole batches.
- Idempotency & request IDs: require clients to send X-Request-ID (UUIDv4) for single calls; for actions that mutate server-side state (rare in our API) require idempotency-key header. Persist X-Request-ID in logs for 90 days and surface it in debug traces.

Deliverables to send back to IntegraHealth by EOD Friday (2026-10-23):
1) SDK snippet (Jordan) that demonstrates: auth interceptor, X-Request-ID injection, and automatic retry with backoff + jitter.
2) Routing doc (Ben) showing region selection, failover behavior, and cost implications.
3) Short runbook (Marissa) for handling 429s during bulk jobs (include recommended client-side behavior and what we'll do server-side).

Jordan — can you also include a minimal sample of how to surface per-item batch failures (suggest a response envelope with item-level statuses and error codes)?

I'll capture these in the HubSpot deal and share the Drive folder.

Thanks,
Marissa

Ack — I'll take SDK snippet and sample response envelope. Plan:
- Provide a TypeScript + Python minimal example that injects X-Request-ID header and exposes a `retryPolicy` config (baseDelay=200ms, maxAttempts=6, jitter=full).
- For batch endpoints: include an example response format: { items: [ {id, status, error_code?} ], retry_after? } and a simple helper to requeue failed ids.
- I'll add an interceptor hook so customers can plug their secret-rotation mechanism.

Ben — can you draft the routing doc and include the fallback policy (region_us -> region_eu, prefer lower cost model when latency bound not strict)?

Will update the Drive folder with snippets by EOD Thursday.
